title: Cap. VI Arg. 1 close: Arminius's own definition — first ratio from theologians' consensus
pass_a_gloss: Finally let Arminius himself be heard; Predestination, he says, is the decree of the good pleasure of God in Christ, by which he has from eternity determined with himself to gift with eternal life the faithful whom he has decreed to gift with faith. Here in predestination a double decree is involved: one, I will to give life to all the faithful: the other, I will to give faith to these certain persons. Both depend on the free and pure mercy of God, neither on foresight faith or any human operation. In vain therefore do they put a condition of foresight faith before predestination, which all Theologians in the very definition of predestination acknowledge to be free, and the spring of faith and of every saving grace. And let this be our first reason, sought from the common consent of Theologians in defining Predestination itself.
pass_b_english: Finally hear Arminius himself: Predestination is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. Predestination involves a double decree: I will give life to all the faithful; and I will give faith to these certain persons. Both depend on God's free pure mercy — neither on foresight faith or any human operation. Vainly then they put a foresight-faith condition before predestination, which all theologians in defining predestination itself acknowledge as free, and the spring of faith and every saving grace. Let this be our first reason — from the common consent of theologians in defining Predestination itself.
source_text: Postremo audiatur ipse Arminius; Praedestinatio, inquit, est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo, quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, vita aeterna donare. Hic in praedestinatione duplex decretum involvitur: unum, Volo cunctis fidelibus dare vitam: alterum, Volo hisce certis personis dare fidem. Utrumque ex Dei gratuita et pura misericordia, neutrum ex praevisa fide aut aliqua humana operatione, dependet. Frustra igitur fidei praevisae conditionem praemittunt praedestinationi, quam omnes Theologi in ipsa praedestinationis definitione agnoscunt esse gratuitam, et fidei omnisque gratiae salutiferae scaturiginem. Atque haec sit prima nostra ratio, petita a communi consensu Theologorum in definienda ipsa Praedestinatione.
